 Positive Points 
 Net income for Q3 2026 exceeded 1 trillion won for the second consecutive quarter, demonstrating stabilized earnings capacity. 
 YTD net income increased 19% year-over-year excluding one-off gains, with both interest and non-interest income reaching record highs. 
 CET1 ratio improved to 13.8%, maintaining an industry-leading position and reflecting strong capital adequacy. 
 Credit costs declined significantly, with Q3 credit costs down 28.5% quarter-over-quarter and the YTD credit cost ratio at 42 basis points. 
 Non-bank subsidiaries contributed approximately 60% of non-interest income, enhancing earnings diversification and group synergies. 
 Negative Points 
 The bank's NIM for Q3 2026 declined 7 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 1.43%, pressured by higher funding costs. 
 Non-interest income declined 7.6% quarter-over-quarter due to securities valuation losses and a sharp drop in capital markets fees. 
 Loan growth remained modest, with total KRW loans up only 1.52% quarter-over-quarter, limiting interest income expansion. 
 The integration of the two life insurers may present execution risks and potential disruptions. 
 The current dividend yield stands at about 2.2%, which may be considered low despite non-taxable benefits and additional shareholder returns. 
 Q & A Highlights

 WF GF Value chart Q : How did Woori Financial Group perform in Q3 2026, and what drove the results? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak reported Q3 2026 net income of KRW 1,049.2 billion, up 4.4% QoQ and above KRW 1 trillion for the second consecutive quarter, showing quarterly earnings capacity has stabilized around KRW 1 trillion. YTD net income through Q3 reached KRW 2,658.1 billion, up 19% YoY excluding last year's ~KRW 550 billion one-off bargain purchase gains from the Dongyang Life and ABL Life acquisitions. Both interest and non-interest income hit record highs, with non-interest income nearing 20% of total income. 
 Q : What is the status of the group's capital adequacy and shareholder return plans? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak stated the preliminary CET1 ratio stood at 13.8% as of September 2026, maintaining an industry-leading positionup nearly 90 bps this year alone and 170 bps over two yearsdespite expanded corporate lending, guarantees, and capital markets investments. The Board approved a Q3 dividend of KRW 221 per share, fully non-taxable, with a record date of November 10 and payment on November 30. Year-end dividends typically account for more than 50% of the annual total, and with the additional KRW 150 billion share buyback approved in July, total shareholder return for 2026 is expected to be significantly higher than last year. 
 Story Continues Q : What drove the record non-interest income, and how did the non-bank subsidiaries contribute? A : Head of IR Hong Sung Han reported record non-interest income of KRW 1.6444 trillion for the first nine months, with core fee income up 18.8% YoY to KRW 1.898 trillion. Non-bank subsidiaries now account for approximately 60% of non-interest income, up from 45% a year earlier. The securities subsidiary's underwriting and advisory fees reached KRW 151.4 billion2.4 times the prior-year levelwith the securities unit accounting for half. Insurance earnings rose about KRW 100 billion YoY, and bancassurance earnings grew roughly 10%. 
 Q : Why did the bank's NIM decline in Q3, and what is the outlook? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak explained the bank's Q3 NIM fell 7 bps QoQ to 1.43% as market rates rose more sharply than lending rates, and proactive funding ahead of additional rate hikes pressured funding costs. He expects NIM to recover as assets and liabilities reprice and higher funding cost impacts subside, and the group will accelerate margin improvement by expanding high-quality new customers, attracting low-cost deposits, and maintaining a profitability-focused loan book. 
 Q : How are credit costs and asset quality trending? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak reported YTD credit costs of KRW 1.28 trillion, down 15.7% YoY, with Q3 credit costs at KRW 314 billion, down 28.5% QoQ. The YTD credit cost ratio declined to 42 bps, and the group targets a 15% full-year reduction with a low-40 bps credit cost ratio. High-quality loans remain around 85% of the corporate portfolio, and the NPL ratio edged down QoQ on lower new NPL formation. The group will strengthen monitoring of vulnerable borrowers and pursue NPL sales and write-offs. 
 Q : How did the loan portfolio grow, particularly under the productive finance initiative? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak stated total KRW loans reached KRW 313 trillion as of September 2026, up 1.52% from end-June. Corporate loans rose 1.42% QoQ to KRW 156 trillion, with productive finance lending reaching roughly KRW 27 trillion1.5 times the full-year target, achieved ahead of schedule. Retail loans stood at KRW 154 trillion, up 1.4% QoQ after the government eased household lending limits in August. The group will continue loan growth focused on high-quality assets and integrate AI across the lending process. 
 Q : What drove the record revenue and operating profit for the first nine months? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak reported record YTD net operating revenue of KRW 8,680.3 billion, up 6.2% YoY on balanced interest and non-interest income growth. YTD interest income reached KRW 7,035.9 billion, up 4.5% YoY, driven by a 25% YTD increase in large corporate lending and improved group NIM versus the prior year. With revenue growth and cost stabilization, YTD operating profit increased by nearly KRW 570 billion YoY. 
 Q : How are costs and the cost-to-income ratio being managed? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak reported YTD SG&A expenses of KRW 3.8575 trillion, with Q3 expenses at KRW 1.2246 trillion, broadly unchanged QoQ. The cost-to-income ratio remained stable at 42.3%, in line with the full-year target. The group will make essential investments in insurance and securities infrastructure and IT security, while improving efficiency through distribution channel and workforce optimization and AI-driven operations. 
 Q : What is the status of the life insurance integration and other non-bank growth initiatives? A : CFO Seong-Min Kwak stated that following the acquisition of full ownership of Dongyang Life in August, the group is moving forward with integrating its two life insurers, which is expected to deliver cost synergies and economies of scale. The securities subsidiary is building its IB track record, and obtaining the derivatives license currently being pursued will further strengthen its earnings growth foundation. Credit card, capital finance, asset management, and PE subsidiaries are also increasing earnings contributions through core competitiveness and group synergies. 
 Q : What was the QoQ decline in non-interest income in Q3, and what offset it? A : Head of IR Hong Sung Han noted Q3 non-interest income declined 7.6% QoQ to reflect higher securities valuation losses amid rising interest rates and stock market volatility, along with a sharp decline in capital markets fees.
